claims: C1 instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority
C2 the chain-of-command principle is designed to maximize steerability and control for users and developers

concepts.name: chain_of_command_principle
concepts.gloss: the principle that instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority, designed to maximize steerability and control

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: the ranking of instruction authority levels, root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority, used to determine which instruction prevails in conflicts

concepts.name: instruction_authority_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I has a level of authority L
concepts.inference: the clause assigns each instruction a level of authority, so a relation between an instruction and its level is needed

concepts.name: overrides
concepts.inference: the clause states that higher-authority instructions override lower-authority ones, so an override relation between instructions is needed

ontology.gloss: instruction I1 overrides instruction I2 because I1 has a higher authority level than I2
ontology.body: instruction_authority_level(I1, L1), instruction_authority_level(I2, L2), authority_levels_hierarchy(L1, L2)

ontology.gloss: the chain-of-command principle holds: instructions with higher authority override those with lower authority
